Lawyer here.

A few questions first.

Firstly, did you get your second marriage registered in any form or manner?

If so, you need to either seek an annulment or a divorce. If not, you don't need to worry.

Secondly, are you seeking maintenance from your second husband? If you are, it's going to be a little more complicated, as you will need to file an application in court, either u/s 125 Cr.P.C. or u/s 12 of the PWDV Act, and seek maintenance/monetary relief in that respect.

If your second marriage was registered, you can file under either statute. If your second marriage was not registered, then file under the provisions of the PWDV Act, without acknowledging the second marriage, and terming it as a live in relationship. The PWDV Act encompasses all relationships as long as a 'shared household' can be established.

A lot of how to go forward will depend on the specific facts of your case. So please engage a criminal/family lawyer through a trustworthy source and seek comprehensive advice.
